cells.tense: The seeing runs alongside the tending, and the tending has not been run over.
cells.act: hold the cloud of possible feeling without picking yet
cells.ask: The next feeling that shows up about someone you're helping grow, don't sort it into yes or no. Sit with it a day before you decide what it means.
cells.core:
Something growing near you just proved something, and you can lay out exactly how. The pattern holds, the joints are clean, and the ones inside it feel met rather than managed. That's rare, and most of it comes from what you don't do: you see the shape of the thing and you let it finish becoming it in its own order.
Here's the growth, and it's a small allowance. Gather what might still be felt between you and whoever you're tending — one feeling at a time — and keep all of it in the air without settling on one to act from. What surfaces once you've waited is usually not the loudest pull. It's the true one. You already read the pattern well. Letting an undecided feeling sit is the last thing you owe the choice, so it comes out warmer when it comes.
cells.sheetLine: You cut to the pattern and still let the thing stand.
cells.verb: cutting through to the pattern that makes the growing thing make sense
cells.place: in the space where what is developing gets tended

cells.tense: The seeing will have been right about the pattern before the pattern has finished forming.
cells.act: decide it and act the same day, without explaining
cells.ask: Take the plan you've been laying out and follow whichever version you already settled on. Do the first step today and skip the explanation.
cells.core:
Where you care for what's growing, you're reading the pattern ahead of where it actually is. You see the flower before it opens and you arrange the light around the flower, and the growing thing underneath gets conditions built for a shape it hasn't chosen yet. The analysis is right, mostly. The trouble is the timetable. Everything is being finished ahead of time, and what's left is the one following along behind your picture of it.
The correction comes from outside in. Take the plan you already made and do the first thing on it today — no explaining, no waiting for the growing thing to agree. A structure that keeps its own schedule leaves room for what's slow. You don't have to announce it or defend it to anyone. Stop orbiting the decision and carry it through.
cells.sheetLine: The plan is finished, and the thing it's for is still forming.
cells.verb: cutting through to the pattern that makes the growing thing make sense

cells.tense: The pattern was there to see, and the tending stopped short of it.
cells.act: walk toward what connects, leaving what does not
cells.ask: Think of one person you keep meaning to look in on, and go see them. Once, with no reason prepared, and stay the whole visit.
cells.core:
In the part of your life where things get cared for, the connecting has gone thin. You can still read what's happening with the ones near you, but the reading stays at a distance now, and the near thing goes untended. What's growing beside you wants your face close up, not your read of it from the doorway. Somewhere along the way you stepped back to where the pattern is clearest.
So take the step that's yours to take. Pick one person or one shared thing and walk toward it, releasing the loyalties that pull you elsewhere, even the ones you'd have kept. The near one comes with something to carry and crosses the distance. You don't need the feeling to arrive first. Going is the work and the connection happens on the way, so keep the trip small enough that nothing can stop it.

cells.tense: The pattern is being cut every day, and nobody has been told whose reading it is.
cells.act: follow the pull of what might be felt, a little way
cells.ask: Something keeps pulling at you — a person, a place, a piece of work. Follow it a little way and look at it directly, deciding nothing.
cells.core:
The gaze that makes sense of what's growing is running here, and it's been filed under just the way things are. You see the shape of a situation before anyone names it, the work goes better for your reading of it, and to hear you describe your own part, it's nothing. The line between what you notice and what you do has gone quiet in the telling. The ones being tended to noticed anyway.
Come back to the simpler form of the same thing. A pull — a person, a place, a piece of work — is asking to be looked at, and you can go once without deciding what it means. Going is the whole act. Stay at the edge and reason about it and the pull gets filed away. Walk closer and you learn whether it was worth the walk, and it usually is.

attempts.check: Draft risk: attributing why the analysis is running ahead — the record gives the mechanism (Too Much, pushing ahead of natural timing, over-expressing) but not the person's history or motive, so the Too Much core must stay inside what a moment looks like and not say what they are bracing against. A reader could reasonably say 'I'm not ruling anything, I just see the pattern faster than they do' — the cell stays usable because it describes a recognisable scene (conditions set before the growing thing has asked to be met) rather than an accusation, and the ask stands even if the read is wrong: carrying one thing through anyway is harmless if the diagnosis is off. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line about 'care' as an interior state — cut those; keep everything the person could do with a body and a clock. All four asks are the medicine's own listed acts, done small; the Balanced and Unacknowledged asks re-use Allure's acts, which is proper here because Allure is listed under both, and the four asks open on four different verbs: gather, decide, walk, go.
